Subject: Keir Starmer (UK PM)
Content:
🧵 MSME DUES LOST IN INSOLVENCY — Where is our Protection?

As an MSME providing essential facility & housekeeping management services, we delivered work honestly, paid our workers, followed every statutory rule — PF, ESIC, wages, insurance.

But when a large corporate client went into insolvency, we waited over 3 years… only to receive 4% of our rightful dues.

No negotiation. No explanation. No access to the process. Just a silent haircut.

✅ Our claim was admitted
 🚫 We were not invited to any committee
 🚫 We couldn’t vote or object
 🚫 No rationale or valuation was shared
 ✅ We got paid ₹4 for every ₹100 owed.

Meanwhile, big secured creditors dictated the plan. And MSMEs like us — who hire some of the most vulnerable workers — were pushed to the bottom of the payout list.

🔍 Under current IBC rules:

- MSMEs are not in the Committee of Creditors
- We rank below banks, tax departments, even employees under Section 53(1) Distribution of Assets during liquidation.
- Once a resolution plan is approved, our dues are extinguished

📣 It’s time for India to walk the talk on MSMEs:
We are called the “backbone of the economy”, but where is the protection?

Can’t the government guarantee MSME dues in such insolvency cases?

Shouldn’t essential service MSMEs be treated on par with ‘workmen’?

This isn’t just about one company. It’s about thousands of MSMEs who will be wiped out if the system doesn’t change.

While I have taken up the issue with the concerned Government Authorities and also Appealed with the NCLT Bench but this needs a serious introspection by the Law as well as Policymakers in India. 

#msme #nclt #corporateinsolvency #PolicySupport #policychange #governmentofindia #safety #IndianEconomy

The Yam as a Symbol of Igbo Culture

Yam holds a central and symbolic place in Igbo culture, reflecting history, agriculture, spirituality, and social life. The root of its significance lies in the Igbo people's long-standing reliance on yam as a staple crop and a cultural emblem of abundance, strength, and communal effort.

Yam is more than food; it marks the cycle of the farming year. The harvest is a time of celebration, gratitude, and communal bonding. The New Yam Festival inaugurates the harvest season, featuring rituals, music, dance, and feasting. It signals readiness to share the bounty and reinforces social ties.

The cultivation of yams is associated with hard work, endurance, and prowess. A successful yam harvest is a visible measure of a family's or individual's strength.
  
In traditional Igbo society, young men demonstrate their capability and readiness for adulthood through their ability to plant, tend, and harvest yams.

Yams represent wealth and social status. The size and quality of a yam harvest can influence the esteem in which a family is held within the community. Sharing and hospitality are integral to Igbo yam culture. Excess harvests are distributed or used to settle disputes, welcome visitors, and honor guests.

Rituals during the yam festival often include offerings to ancestors and spiritual entities, acknowledging the earth’s generosity and seeking continued fertility.

Covered Call is like renting out your house.
You already own the house (stock).

If the tenant wants to buy your house at a fixed price (strike price) later, you must sell it — even if the market price is higher.

Content:
⚡ AAAR Upholds ITC on Electrical Installations Outside Factory
[TS-839-AAAR(GUJ)-2025-GST]

Gujarat Appellate Authority for Advance Ruling (AAAR) upheld ITC eligibility on wires, cables, and electrical equipment installed outside factory premises for electricity transmission, rejecting the Department’s appeal.

⚖️ AAAR Ruling Highlights:

•ITC Allowed: The installation qualifies as “plant and machinery”, as it directly facilitates power supply to manufacturing operations.
•Not Immovable Property:
•The underground cables were not permanently affixed to the earth and could be removed for maintenance.
•Hence, they don’t fall within exclusions for immovable property.
•Circular Support: Relied on CBIC Circular No. 219/13/2024-GST, clarifying ITC availability on components (like ducts/manholes) forming part of telecom/utility infrastructure.

🧩 Key Takeaway:

The ruling reinforces that functional nexus and business use are the true tests for ITC eligibility — location alone is not determinative.

Subject: Keir Starmer (UK PM)
Content:
💼 Gujarat HC Dismisses Revenue’s Plea to Cancel Bail — ECL Deposit Held as Valid Compliance ⚖️

🔹 Key Case Facts:
•Condition: Respondent was required to deposit ₹90 lakhs within 7 days as part of bail terms.
•Revenue’s Argument: The deposit was made in the company’s ECL, not through Form GST DRC-03, and hence didn’t reach the Government exchequer.
•Assessee’s Rebuttal:
•₹90 lakhs was debited from his bank account and credited to the Government account.
•Section 49 of the CGST Act treats credit in ECL as payment to the Government.
•Filing DRC-03 would imply admission of liability, potentially affecting the right to appeal.

⚖️ Court’s Findings:
•Referring to Section 49 and the Arya Cotton Industries judgment, the Court reiterated that once payment is credited to the Government account, liability stands discharged.
•Revenue’s apprehension that the amount could be re-utilised was found unfounded, as the accused undertook not to use or seek refund.
•The Court emphasised that bail cancellation requires supervening circumstances or violation of conditions, neither of which existed here.

Content:
We don’t often share numbers, but with yesterday’s announcement it felt right to provide a bit of context. Alongside the employee tender, we shared that ElevenLabs has now reached $200M ARR. Our valuation is tied to our growth and revenue. In AI, things can shift quickly - both for better and worse - so we measure ourselves by what’s real: the trust of our customers, the speed of our iteration & progress, and the fit of our products in the market.

A quick look-back:
- Early 2022: ElevenLabs founded
- 2022-11: launched closed beta
- 2023-01: launched publicly
- 2024-10: crossed $100M ARR
- 2025-08: crossed $200M ARR
- 2026-01: aiming for $300M ARR

Three years on, we’re still heads down and not taking anything for granted. Each milestone was driven by our customers, and a small team working with high intent - doing the best work of their lives - alongside companies bold enough to build at the frontier.

Now - back to building.

Content:
August Research & Product Roundup at ElevenLabs - not a quiet summer! Proud of our research team for once again pushing the frontier and the product team for the continuous incredible pace.

Eleven Music is live. First high-quality, fully licensed model built for broad commercial use. After shipping natural Text to Speech in 2022, launching Eleven v3 (first controllable TTS model), and releasing Eleven Scribe, our Speech to Text model that is able to outperform those from OpenAI/Google, it’s amazing to see our team ship something this strong again. With simple prompts you can create original music - film score, game cue, or a background soundscape in a conversational app. And, of course, it’s available via API too. We can’t wait to see what people build.

Research is just our foundation. Where we spend most of our time is expanding our platform offerings further: for building fast and reliable conversational agents or creating immersive and beautiful narrations or voiceovers. Recent updates below.

Conversational AI // Agents platform
- IVR navigation: let agents follow existing IVR logic
- SDKs: React Native and Kotlin for easier developer building
- Chat mode: we now support text-only agents too
- Orchestration and reliability improvements across all agents

Creative platform
- APIs: Eleven v3 and Eleven Music available
- Video-to-Music in Studio: automatically add a music track to a video
- The platform is now localized to French, Hindi, Japanese, Polish, Portuguese, Spanish and Swedish

Agents Platform

Creative Platform

- We introduced Productions for ordering human-edited dubbing, captions, transcripts, and audiobooks directly in ElevenLabs
- Launched Voice Remixing (alpha) for reimagining your own or designed voices.
- SFX v2 supports higher quality, seamless looping, 30s duration, 48 kHz, an expanded library, and Studio integration

Content:
Early Life #LalBahadurShastriJayanti

Born: 2 October 1904 in Mughalsarai, Uttar Pradesh (same date as Mahatma Gandhi’s birthday).

His father, a school teacher, died when Shastri was very young, and he grew up in humble conditions.

He dropped his caste-based surname "Srivastava" early in life as a stand against caste discrimination.

Education & Freedom Struggle
Inspired by Mahatma Gandhi and the independence movement at a young age.

Joined the non-cooperation movement in 1921, was imprisoned for participating in protests against the British.

Studied at Kashi Vidyapeeth, where he was given the title “Shastri” (scholar).

 Political Career
After independence, he served in various ministries including Railways, Transport, and Communications.

Known for being honest, humble, and hardworking.

In 1964, after Jawaharlal Nehru’s death, he became the 2nd Prime Minister of India.

Contributions
Gave the famous slogan “Jai Jawan Jai Kisan” (Hail the soldier, Hail the farmer), emphasizing food security and defense.

Promoted the Green Revolution in India to make the country self-sufficient in food grains.

Strengthened India’s defense forces after the 1962 war with China.

 Indo-Pak War (1965)

Led the country during the 1965 India-Pakistan war.

His calm leadership boosted national morale.

Ceasefire agreement was signed in Tashkent, USSR (now Uzbekistan).

Death
Died suddenly on 11 January 1966 in Tashkent, a day after signing the peace agreement with Pakistan’s Ayub Khan.

His death remains surrounded by mystery, with debates about whether it was natural or not.

Legacy
Remembered as a leader of simplicity, integrity, and determination.

The Shastri National Memorial in New Delhi preserves his memory.

His birthday (2nd October) is observed along with Gandhi Jayanti as a national holiday in India.
